retrieved_context: Chicagoland Sports Hall of Fame: The Chicagoland Sports Hall of Fame, located in the Hawthorne Race Course, in Stickney/Cicero, near Chicago, Illinois, honors sports greats associated with the Chicago metropolitan area.  It was founded in 1979 as a trailer owned by the Olympia Brewing Company parked at Soldier Field in Chicago.  The Chicago Park District took over the exhibits in 1983.  From 1988 the exhibits were displayed in Mike Ditka's restaurant until the restaurant closed in 1991.  The Hall of Fame moved to the Maryville Academy in Des Plaines in 1996 and has operated under the guidance of Father John P. Smyth since that time.  As of 2008, it was operating at Hawthorne.

The Gogo Building: The Gogo Building, formerly known as the River Center, is located at 111 N. Canal Street in the West Loop community area of Chicago, Illinois.  Originally constructed as a warehouse in the early 1900s, the vintage, loft-style building is now home to various commercial tenants, most notably Gogo Inflight Internet, as seen by their logo on the cube topping the building.  Other tenants include Twitter, Uber, Vivid Seats, Fieldglass, Potbelly and Solstice.  The building is one of the best surviving examples in downtown Chicago of the once vibrant industrial district along the Chicago River.

Clyde Emrich: Clyde Emrich (born April 6, 1931 Chicago, Illinois) is a former Olympic weightlifter for the United States.  He was also a long-time strength coach for the Chicago Bears, who in 2008 named their weight room after him.  He is a member of the Chicagoland Sports Hall of Fame.
